region: North and Central America, Europe and Asia; main lumber species are black walnut (eastern North America) and English walnut (Europe/Asia)
description: Walnut is a dark, prized furniture hardwood, mainly black walnut (Juglans nigra) in North America and English or European walnut (Juglans regia). Woodworkers use it for fine furniture, gunstocks, veneer, turning, and accents, and it is often finished without stain for its chocolate-brown color.

hazards.summary: IARC classifies all wood dust as carcinogenic to humans, mainly linked to cancer of the nasal cavity and sinuses after long-term heavy exposure. This applies to every species, so dust control matters whatever you cut.
ACGIH names walnut dust as a suspected human carcinogen (A2). The listing says walnut without naming a species.

One worker developed asthma from Central American walnut (Juglans olanchana) dust, confirmed by inhalation challenge; no IgE antibodies were found, so the mechanism is unclear. This is not black or English walnut, and we found no confirmed asthma reports for those species.
The UK HSE lists sneezing and runny or blocked nose (rhinitis) for walnut, excluding African walnut. It does not name the Juglans species.
A Finnish clinic series found two workers whose dermatitis reacted to walnut dust on patch testing. The abstract does not say which walnut species.

Juglone in green walnut husks can stain skin brown and cause blistering irritation, and the UK HSE notes dermatitis from walnut nut shells and roots. This comes from the nuts, husks, and roots rather than dry lumber.

exposure_limits.note: 8-hour time-weighted average, as restated by OSHA

known_compounds.name: juglone
known_compounds.role: skin irritant and stain in green walnut husks

related_species_note: 'African walnut' (Lovoa trichilioides) and 'Brazilian walnut' or imbuia (Ocotea porosa) are not Juglans; check their own pages. WFO now treats Juglans olanchana as a synonym of Juglans pyriformis.

notes_internal: No species-specific respiratory or dermatology primary paper found for Juglans nigra or J. regia wood dust in PubMed (searched juglone, Juglans nigra, walnut wood/sawdust). Bush-1983 is J. olanchana (WFO: synonym of J. pyriformis) and the IgE test was negative, though challenge was positive; level 1 per our criteria. Estlander-2001 walnut species not stated in abstract; reviewer may want full text. Juglone hazard is from husks/nuts, not wood; source_part left blank because the schema has no 'husk' value. Black walnut shavings are known to be toxic to horses (veterinary literature, e.g. PMID 2061431); not added as a human hazard. Soylu 2023 (PMID 37040275, juglone bullous dermatitis) found but closed access, not used. Walnut food allergy (nut proteins) is not a wood-dust hazard and was excluded. Absence of reports for a hazard is not evidence that this wood is safe.
